patients.summary: Graduate student who joined at 21 with known genital HSV-2 on episodic valacyclovir. Over 2025-2026 she has treated gonococcal cervicitis, HSV cervicitis seen by gynecology, an admission for chlamydial PID with a tubo-ovarian complex and a failing pregnancy of unknown location, a community-acquired pneumonia, and a post-clindamycin severe C. difficile admission; well at her June 2026 physical.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
21 yo F here to establish care. Starting her last undergraduate year and planning on graduate school locally, so wanted a doctor in town.

PMH: genital herpes, HSV-2, confirmed by swab PCR at college health spring 2020. Gets 2-3 outbreaks a year, small cluster, uses valacyclovir 500 bid x3 days when it starts and it settles within a few days. Not interested in daily suppression right now. Otherwise healthy. No hospitalizations.
PSH: none.
Meds: valacyclovir prn only.
Allergies: penicillin. Told as a child she reacted to it; she doesn't know what the reaction was.
FH: mom with high blood pressure, dad has type 2 diabetes, younger sister has asthma.
SH: student. Lives in an apartment with a roommate. Never smoked. Alcohol socially, a drink or two a week. Sexually active, uses condoms most of the time. Not currently on hormonal contraception.
GYN: menses monthly, regular. No Pap yet.

ROS negative except as above.

Exam: well-appearing. HEENT normal, no adenopathy. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin without rash. Mood and affect normal. Pelvic deferred, will do with Pap at next physical.

A/P
1. Genital HSV-2, infrequent recurrences. Continue episodic valacyclovir, refills on file. Reviewed that suppressive therapy is an option if outbreaks become frequent, and that it reduces but does not eliminate transmission.
2. Health maintenance: screening labs today (CBC, CMP, lipids), one-time HIV and hep C, RPR, urine GC/CT. Will get vaccine history from college records; believes HPV series is done. Pap next year at her physical. Flu shot in the fall.
3. Penicillin allergy, reaction unknown. Could consider allergy testing at some point.

RTC 1 year for physical, sooner prn.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Caitlin, everything from Tuesday came back fine: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, and cholesterol are all normal, and the HIV, hepatitis C, syphilis, gonorrhea and chlamydia tests were all negative. Nothing to do. Good to meet you.

documents.title: College health service records
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Records from college student health service, 14 pages, received by secure email and scanned.

Contents: immunization record (childhood MMR and varicella x2 each, Tdap and MenACWY at 13, MenACWY booster 2018, 2-dose HPV series 2014, hepatitis B series in infancy per pediatric record, COVID primary series 2021). Visit 03/2020: painful vulvar ulcers, swab PCR positive for HSV-2, treated with valacyclovir. Two later visits for recurrences, episodic valacyclovir. Annual GC/CT screens negative. Allergy listed as penicillin, reaction not recorded.

Immunizations abstracted to chart. Forwarded to PCP.

documents.title: Immunization visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In for flu and bivalent COVID booster. Screening questions negative, no egg or vaccine reactions. Flu 0.5 mL IM left arm, COVID 0.3 mL IM right arm. VIS reviewed. Observed 15 min, felt fine, left with arm soreness instructions.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
22 yo here for yearly exam. Started her master's program this month, busy but good. HSV: two outbreaks since last fall, both brief with the episodic valacyclovir. No other concerns. Same partner situation as before, uses condoms.
No daily meds. Allergy PCN.
Smoking never. EtOH 1-2/wk. Exercises - runs a few times a week.

Exam: NAD. HEENT clear, neck supple, no thyromegaly. Cardiac regular, no murmurs. Lungs clear bilaterally. Abd soft, NT. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, no lesions today. Vaginal walls normal, cervix normal appearing, Pap obtained. Bimanual without tenderness or masses. Skin normal.

A/P
- Well visit. Pap today (first one). Urine GC/CT.
- HSV-2 stable on episodic tx.
- Flu and updated COVID when the clinic gets supply.
- Tdap due next year (last 2014).
Follow up 1 yr.

Second year of her master's, working in a research lab most days. Sleeping OK, some stress around deadlines, nothing she can't manage. HSV - maybe two flares this year, valacyclovir works. Started dating someone new this fall, condoms most of the time. Asked for STI testing, which we do yearly anyway.

Meds: valacyclovir prn. NKA except PCN.
Smoking: never. Alcohol: 1-2 drinks weekly.

Vitals reviewed, normal. General: healthy-appearing. Eyes, ears, throat normal. Neck no nodes. Heart: S1 S2 normal, no murmur, rate regular. Lungs: clear. Abd: soft, nontender, no organomegaly. Ext: warm, no swelling. Skin: no rashes. Psych: pleasant, appropriate.

Assessment/plan:
Adult wellness exam. Tdap today, 10 yrs since the adolescent dose. GC/CT urine, HIV and RPR repeated given new partner. Pap was 2023, next 2026. PHQ-2 1, fine. Flu and COVID in October.
Genital HSV - episodic valacyclovir, refills fine.

documents.title: Acute Visit - Discharge
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: About 10 days of more vaginal discharge than usual, thicker, slightly yellow. No odor she notices. No itching, no pelvic pain, no pain with sex, no fever, no urinary burning. No sores - says this doesn't feel like her herpes. One partner since last fall. LMP 5/12, normal.

O: Afebrile, vitals fine. Ext genitalia normal, no ulcers or vesicles. Speculum: yellow mucopurulent discharge at the os, cervix otherwise unremarkable, no bleeding with swab. Bimanual: no cervical motion tenderness, no adnexal tenderness. Urine hCG neg.

A/P: Mucopurulent cervicitis. Cervical NAAT for GC/CT sent, HIV and RPR drawn. She would rather wait for results than take empiric antibiotics today, given the penicillin allergy history and wanting to know what she's treating. Reasonable since she has no PID signs - will call with results in 1-2 days and treat promptly. Abstain until then.

documents.title: Results call - gonorrhea
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt with results. Gonorrhea NAAT positive, chlamydia negative, HIV and RPR nonreactive. Treatment is ceftriaxone 500 mg IM once. Discussed PCN allergy: unknown childhood reaction, and cross-reactivity with ceftriaxone is low; she agrees to proceed with observation after. Nurse visit tomorrow. Partner needs evaluation and treatment - she'll tell him today, info sheet sent through portal. No sex for 7 days after both are treated. Retest in 3 months. Reportable, lab notifies DPH.

documents.title: Ceftriaxone IM
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Ceftriaxone 500 mg reconstituted with lidocaine per protocol, given IM R ventrogluteal at 0925. Pt observed 30 min given penicillin allergy history: no hives, no wheeze, no lightheadedness. BP and HR stable at end of observation. Reviewed partner treatment and abstinence for 7 days. Left ambulatory. Added recheck reminder for late August.

documents.title: Bleeding after sex
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, for about two weeks I've had some bleeding after sex, not every time but more than once, and a yellow discharge again. No pain. It's honestly freaking me out a bit. Period was normal earlier this month. Should I come in or see a gynecologist?

documents.title: Reply and referral
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called her back. Bleeding after intercourse plus discharge needs a speculum exam and testing; given it's recurrent cervical symptoms I'd like gynecology to see her and they can do colposcopy on the spot if needed. Referral placed, front desk to help get it within 1-2 weeks. She was also due for the gonorrhea recheck, gyn can do the NAAT. If pelvic pain, fever or heavy bleeding, come in same day.

documents.title: Gynecology Consultation
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Outpatient gynecology consultation
Visit date: 09/02/2025
Referring: primary care

Reason: two weeks of postcoital bleeding and yellow discharge.

Ms. Keane is a 24 year old G0 graduate student who for about two weeks has had spotting after intercourse on several occasions along with a yellowish vaginal discharge. Intercourse is not painful. She is quite upset by the bleeding. She has had a single partner for roughly a year. LMP about three weeks ago, typical flow.

History: genital HSV-2 with infrequent recurrences, episodic valacyclovir. Gonococcal cervicitis treated with IM ceftriaxone in May of this year. No surgeries.
Medications: valacyclovir as needed only.
Allergies: penicillin.
Family: mother hypertension; father type 2 diabetes; sister asthma.
Social: never smoker, about 1-2 drinks a week, graduate student.

Exam: vital signs normal. External genitalia without ulcers. Speculum: cervix is friable and bleeds on contact, with mucopurulent discharge from the os. Bimanual: no cervical motion tenderness, uterus and adnexa normal and nontender.

Urine hCG negative. Cervical NAAT sent for chlamydia, gonorrhea and trichomonas; cervical swab sent for HSV PCR.

Impression: cervicitis with contact bleeding; infectious causes being tested. Cervical cytology was normal in 2023.
Plan: will contact her with results and treat accordingly. Condoms in the meantime.

Thank you for this referral.
Gynecology

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily for 5 days

documents.title: Gynecology results letter
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Results from 09/02/2025 visit:
- Chlamydia NAAT, cervical: not detected
- Gonorrhea NAAT, cervical: not detected (serves as her post-treatment retest)
- Trichomonas NAAT: not detected
- HSV PCR, cervical swab: HSV-2 detected

Impression: viral cervicitis due to herpes simplex type 2, in a patient with known genital HSV-2. This explains the friable cervix and contact bleeding.
Plan: valacyclovir 500 mg twice daily for 5 days, sent to her pharmacy. Discussed the option of daily suppressive therapy if recurrences increase. Return if bleeding continues after the course. Patient informed by phone.
Allergies: penicillin.

documents.title: Outside results reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed gyn letter. HSV-2 cervicitis, GC retest negative. Problem list updated. Referral closed.

documents.title: Question about gyn result
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The gynecologist said the bleeding was from herpes on my cervix. I didn't know that could happen without sores. Is this something that's going to keep happening? I'm taking the pills.

documents.title: Reply
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good question. Yes, HSV can shed and inflame the cervix without any outside sores, which is why it caused bleeding you could see but not feel. It usually settles with the course you're on. If it comes back often, a daily low dose of valacyclovir is a good option and we can talk about it anytime. The gonorrhea retest was negative, which is good news.

documents.title: Influenza and COVID vaccination
documents.author: RN
documents.body: 2025-26 influenza and COVID vaccines given IM, left and right deltoid respectively. Screening negative. Observed, no issues. Bleeding resolved after the gyn course per pt.

events.reason: Severe lower abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding

reports.text:
Transabdominal and transvaginal pelvic ultrasound. Indication: positive hCG, pelvic pain, bleeding.
Uterus: anteverted, normal size. Endometrium 7 mm, no intrauterine gestational sac, yolk sac or embryo.
Right adnexa: complex mass measuring 4.6 x 3.8 cm, thick-walled with internal septations and low-level echoes, inseparable from the right ovary, with surrounding hyperemia on color flow. No extrauterine gestational sac, yolk sac or embryo seen.
Left ovary normal in size and appearance.
Small amount of anechoic free fluid in the pelvis, without clot or echogenic debris. No fluid in the hepatorenal space.
reports.conclusion: No intrauterine pregnancy. Complex right adnexal mass 4.6 x 3.8 cm, favored tubo-ovarian complex in this clinical setting; no adnexal gestation identified. Small simple pelvic free fluid. Correlate with serial hCG.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department
Arrival 11/28/2025 13:40

CC: sudden bad lower belly pain and vaginal bleeding

HPI: 24F G1 by today's test, known genital HSV-2, gonococcal cervicitis treated with IM ceftriaxone about 6 months ago, seen by gynecology in September for cervical bleeding and discharge. Today developed sudden, severe lower abdominal pain this morning, worse on the right, with vaginal bleeding. LMP 7 weeks ago. Unaware she was pregnant.

Meds: none daily. Allergies: penicillin.

Exam: pale, uncomfortable. BP 84/50, HR 116, T 37.4. Oropharynx: posterior pharynx mildly erythematous, no exudate. Abdomen: diffusely tender, most marked RLQ, with rebound and voluntary guarding. Pelvic per gyn.

Data: urine bHCG positive; quant hCG 412. WBC 15.8, Hgb 11.2, lactate 2.4, CRP 96. CMP unremarkable. TVUS: no IUP, small simple free fluid, 4.6 cm complex R adnexal mass, no adnexal gestation seen. Cervical and throat NAATs sent. Blood cultures x2.

Course: 2 L LR, BP up to 104/64, HR 98. Gyn at bedside; ectopic considered, but low hCG, no extrauterine gestation, simple fluid only and stable after fluids, with imaging favoring tubo-ovarian complex. Started ceftriaxone, metronidazole and azithromycin.

Impression: pelvic inflammatory disease with right tubo-ovarian complex, early pregnancy of unknown location, sepsis responding to fluids.
Disposition: admitted to gynecology.

Addendum 11/29: cervical and pharyngeal chlamydia NAAT positive, gonorrhea negative. HIV and RPR nonreactive.

events.reason: Pelvic inflammatory disease with tubo-ovarian complex

medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth twice daily to complete 14 days
Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily to complete 14 days

documents.title: Gynecology Discharge Summary
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Admitted 11/28/2025, discharged 12/01/2025

Diagnoses:
1. Acute pelvic inflammatory disease, Chlamydia trachomatis, with right tubo-ovarian complex
2. Pharyngeal chlamydia infection
3. Early pregnancy of unknown location, failing (hCG 412 -> 236)

Hospital course: Presented with acute lower abdominal pain, bleeding and hypotension that corrected with IV fluid. Ultrasound showed no intrauterine pregnancy and a complex right adnexal mass consistent with tubo-ovarian complex, with only simple free fluid. Ectopic gestation was not seen and the clinical picture stayed stable, so she was managed medically with close hCG follow-up. Treated with IV ceftriaxone 1 g daily and IV metronidazole; azithromycin 1 g single dose given at admission while pregnancy status was uncertain. hCG fell from 412 to 236 at 48 hours, consistent with a failing pregnancy. Afebrile throughout, tenderness much improved by day 3, tolerating diet. Penicillin allergy noted; tolerated ceftriaxone, as she did in May.

Discharge medications: doxycycline 100 mg PO BID and metronidazole 500 mg PO BID to complete 14 days total. Ibuprofen as needed for cramping.
Allergies: penicillin.

Follow-up: gynecology clinic 12/08 with repeat hCG, weekly until negative. Repeat pelvic ultrasound in about 6 weeks. Partner to be treated before resuming intercourse. Test of reinfection in 3 months. Primary care within one week.
Return precautions given: worsening pain, fever, heavy bleeding, fainting.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Transitional care call after gyn admission 11/28-12/1. Pt reached. Pain mild, cramping only, taking ibuprofen once or twice a day. Spotting, light. No fever. Has doxycycline and metronidazole, taking with food, some nausea with the metronidazole but keeping them down. Reminded no alcohol with metronidazole. Gyn appt 12/8 for hCG. PCP visit booked 12/4. Partner has an appointment for treatment.

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after 3-day gyn admission for chlamydial PID with a right tubo-ovarian complex; ED found a positive pregnancy test with no IUP, hCG 412 then 236, being followed as a failing pregnancy. Also pharyngeal chlamydia. Discharge summary reviewed.

Today: cramping is mild, needs ibuprofen maybe once a day. Light spotting. No fevers. On day 7 of 14 of doxycycline + metronidazole, some queasiness but taking everything. Pregnancy was unexpected and she says she's sad and relieved at the same time; has support from a close friend and her sister. Partner is getting treated.

Exam: afebrile, BP normal. Looks well. Abdomen soft, mild tenderness right lower quadrant, no rebound. Throat clear.

A/P
1. Chlamydial PID with R TO complex - improving on oral therapy. Finish 14 days. Gyn has hCG 12/8 and repeat ultrasound in January. Abstain until both she and partner are done with treatment. Retest GC/CT (genital and throat) late February.
2. Pharyngeal chlamydia - covered by the doxycycline.
3. Pregnancy of unknown location, hCG falling - gyn following to zero. Bleeding precautions reviewed.
4. HSV cervicitis from September - resolved, no further bleeding before this. Removing from active list.
5. Mood: PHQ-2 of 2, understandable after a hard week. Offered counseling resources through the university; she'll reach out if she wants a referral. Check in at next visit.

documents.title: Gynecology follow-up note
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body: Gynecology clinic, visit 12/08/2025. Post-discharge check after PID/TOC and failing pregnancy of unknown location. Cramping minimal, bleeding nearly stopped, afebrile. Abdomen soft with minimal right adnexal tenderness on bimanual. Serum hCG 61, down from 236. Completing doxycycline and metronidazole. Plan: weekly hCG until negative; pelvic ultrasound early January. Allergies: penicillin.

documents.title: Gynecology result letter
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body: hCG on 12/22/2025: less than 5 mIU/mL. The pregnancy has fully resolved; no further hCG testing needed. Ultrasound scheduled 01/07/2026 to confirm the right adnexal complex has cleared. Patient notified.

reports.text:
Transvaginal pelvic ultrasound, follow-up of right adnexal complex.
Uterus anteverted, normal size and contour. Endometrium 5 mm, homogeneous.
Right ovary 3.1 x 2.0 cm, normal follicles, normal flow. No adnexal mass.
Left ovary 2.9 x 1.8 cm, normal.
No free fluid.
reports.conclusion: Normal pelvic ultrasound. Previously seen right adnexal complex has resolved.

documents.title: Gynecology ultrasound follow-up
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body: Follow-up visit 01/07/2026. Feels well, no pelvic pain, normal period in late December. Exam nontender. Ultrasound today normal with resolution of the right tubo-ovarian complex. PID resolved clinically and on imaging. She is returning to primary care for the 3-month chlamydia retest. No gynecology follow-up needed beyond routine care.

documents.title: Same-day visit: cough, fever
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Texted this morning, worked in late morning.

4 days of cough, now productive of yellow sputum, fevers to 101-102 at home, chills, tired. Some right-sided chest discomfort when she coughs hard. No shortness of breath at rest. Roommate had a cold last week. No recent travel.
No daily meds. Allergy PCN.

T 38.4, SpO2 96% RA, other vitals in flowsheet. Tired but not toxic. Speaking full sentences. Throat mildly injected. Lungs: crackles at the right base, no wheeze, otherwise good air movement. Heart regular, tachy-ish with fever.

Rapid flu neg, COVID PCR neg.
CXR (read below): right lower lobe airspace opacity.

A/P: Community-acquired pneumonia, RLL, outpatient-appropriate (young, no comorbidities, sats fine, CURB-65 0). Penicillin allergy so doxycycline 100 bid x5 days. Fluids, acetaminophen. Expect fever to break in 48-72h; message me Friday with an update, sooner if short of breath or not improving. Follow-up visit in about a month, which can line up with her chlamydia retest.

reports.text: PA and lateral views of the chest. Patchy airspace opacity in the right lower lobe, posterior basal region on the lateral view. No pleural effusion. No pneumothorax. Heart size normal. Mediastinal contours normal. Osseous structures intact.
reports.conclusion: Right lower lobe airspace opacity consistent with pneumonia in the appropriate clinical setting.

documents.title: Update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Fever broke yesterday, still coughing but way less. Feeling human again. Last doxy pill is tomorrow night.

documents.title: Reply
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Great, that's the course we hoped for. The cough can hang on for a few weeks. Front desk will set up the visit in late February.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Pneumonia f/u: cough gone for about 10 days, energy back, running again. No fevers.
PID: gyn ultrasound in January was normal, hCG negative in December. No pelvic pain. Period regular.
Here for the 3-month chlamydia retest, urine and throat swab. Partner was treated in December.
Mood better than in December, PHQ deferred today, she declines counseling for now.

Vitals normal, SpO2 normal. Lungs clear throughout, no crackles. Abdomen benign.

- CAP resolved clinically. No repeat imaging needed at her age with full recovery.
- PID resolved per gyn.
- Chlamydia test of reinfection: urine and pharyngeal NAAT sent. Will message results.
- Physical due in late summer; Pap due this year too.

documents.title: Hospital Medicine Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital, internal medicine service
Admitted 03/25/2026, discharged 03/28/2026

Principal diagnosis: severe Clostridioides difficile infection, no toxic megacolon

HPI: 25 year old woman with genital HSV-2 and prior gonococcal cervicitis and chlamydial PID, both treated. Took clindamycin 300 mg four times daily for 10 days for a dental abscess (prescribed by her dentist, finished 3/11). About a week later she developed watery diarrhea, now 6-7 times daily and for the past day streaked with blood, with two days of severe crampy lower abdominal pain. Mildly nauseated, no vomiting, no fever. Takes no regular medications.
Allergies: penicillin.

Exam on admission: uncomfortable, afebrile. Abdomen soft, tender left lower quadrant, no rebound or guarding, bowel sounds active. No distension.

Data: WBC and creatinine normal. Albumin 2.9. Stool C. difficile PCR positive with toxin positive. Abdominal imaging not performed; no distension or peritoneal signs.

Course: classified as severe given bloody diarrhea, frequency and hypoalbuminemia despite a normal white count. Supportive care with IV fluids and antiemetic as needed, diet advanced. Oral vancomycin 125 mg four times daily started 3/25. Stool frequency down to 3 per day without blood by discharge, cramping mild. Contact precautions observed.

Discharge medications: vancomycin 125 mg PO four times daily to complete 10 days (through 4/3).
Instructions: hand washing with soap and water at home, bleach-based cleaner for bathroom. Avoid unnecessary antibiotics; tell any prescriber, including the dentist, about this infection. Return for fever, worsening pain, distension, or more than 6 stools per day.
Follow-up: primary care within 1 week.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: TCM outreach after 3/25-3/28 admission for C. diff. Pt reports 2-3 loose-to-soft stools per day, no blood since Friday. Eating bland foods, drinking well. Taking oral vancomycin 4x daily, has enough to finish 4/3. Reviewed handwashing (soap, not gel) and bathroom cleaning. Video follow-up 4/2 with PCP.

documents.title: Telehealth follow-up after admission
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, pt at her apartment, consented.

Admitted 3/25-3/28 for severe C. diff after a 10-day clindamycin course from her dentist. Discharge summary reviewed: C. diff PCR and toxin positive, albumin 2.9, WBC and kidney function normal, on oral vancomycin.

Now 2 soft stools a day, no blood, cramps gone. Appetite coming back. Thinks she lost a few pounds. Last vancomycin dose tomorrow.

Looks well on video, no distress.

A/P
C. difficile infection, severe, improving. Finish vancomycin tomorrow. About 1 in 5 people have a recurrence in the next 2 months; if diarrhea returns (3+ loose stools a day), message the same day and we'll test and treat - don't use loperamide. Avoid antibiotics unless truly needed; clindamycin noted as the trigger, please flag with her dentist. Weight at physical. Doing well otherwise: pneumonia and PID both resolved, chlamydia retest negative.

conditions.label: Severe Clostridioides difficile infection without toxic megacolon

documents.title: Checking in
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just wanted to say I'm back to normal, no diarrhea since finishing the vancomycin. Do I need any test to make sure it's gone?

documents.title: Reply
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad to hear it. No test needed - we don't retest when you feel well, because the test can stay positive without infection. Only if symptoms come back. I've moved it to your past history.

reports.text: Specimen: cervical, liquid-based preparation. Adequacy: satisfactory for evaluation; endocervical/transformation zone component present. Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. No organisms identified.

documents.title: Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
25 yo F, yearly visit, a few months early by her request.

Interval: hard winter - PID admission in November (failing pregnancy of unknown location, resolved), pneumonia in January, C. diff in March after clindamycin. All resolved. No diarrhea since April. Weight back to about where she was. HSV quiet, one short flare in May treated with her valacyclovir. No pelvic pain, periods regular.

Meds: valacyclovir prn. Allergies: penicillin (tolerated ceftriaxone twice).
PMH/PSH reviewed: no surgeries.
FH: mother HTN, father T2DM, sister asthma.
SH: grad student, same partner. Never smoker. 1-2 drinks/week. AUDIT-C 2.

Exam: well, BMI normal. HEENT normal. Neck without adenopathy or thyromegaly. Lungs clear. Heart: regular, no murmur. Abdomen soft and nontender, no masses. Pelvic: external normal; cervix normal, no friability, no discharge; Pap collected. Bimanual nontender, no adnexal fullness. Skin clear.

A/P
1. Preventive: Pap today (3 yrs since 2023). Urine GC/CT, HIV, RPR given this year's infections. CBC/CMP to confirm recovery (albumin was low in March). PHQ-2 0. Vaccines: Tdap 2024, flu and COVID in the fall.
2. Genital HSV-2, infrequent recurrences, episodic valacyclovir.
3. History of C. diff - antibiotic stewardship, clindamycin flagged as the precipitant in her chart.
4. History of gonorrhea and chlamydial PID, treated, retests negative.
Follow-up early fall for flu shot and check-in.
